Vector of MaxIntensityData pairs used as time/value samples for timed interpolation.

functions.name: distance
functions.description: Computes the distance between two 3D vectors. Forward-declared here and used by ConstVelLinearInterpolator to measure segment lengths; likely Euclidean distance. Implementation is not provided in this header.
requirements: lhs and rhs must be valid glm::vec3 objects.
Behavior and metric are unknown beyond typical distance semantics; callers should expect a non-negative float result.
Must be linked/provided elsewhere; otherwise linking will fail.

functions.name: GetValue
functions.description: Extracts the value component from a LightVectorData element. Intended for use with TimedLinearInterpolator to retrieve the interpolated data (glm::vec4). Implementation is not provided here; by convention it should return the first element of the pair.
requirements: data must be a valid LightVectorData (typedef std::pair<glm::vec4, float>).
Function must be defined elsewhere and accessible at link time.

functions.name: GetTime
functions.description: Extracts the time/weight component from a LightVectorData element as a float in [0,1] for TimedLinearInterpolator. Implementation is not provided here; by convention it should return the second element of the pair.
requirements: data must be a valid LightVectorData (typedef std::pair<glm::vec4, float>).
The returned time/weight is expected to be within [0.0f, 1.0f] (asserted by TimedLinearInterpolator::SetValues).
Function must be defined elsewhere and accessible at link time.

functions.name: Framework::WeightedLinearInterpolator::NumSegments
functions.description: Returns the number of linear interpolation segments implied by the loaded control values. With N values, there are max(N-1, 0) segments.
requirements: Valid only after values have been populated into the interpolator (e.g., via a SetValues method of a derived class).
ValueType is a template parameter; no specific constraints for this method.

functions.name: Framework::WeightedLinearInterpolator::Interpolate
functions.description: Performs piecewise-linear interpolation over the stored control values using their per-entry weights as breakpoints. Returns a default-constructed ValueType if no values are loaded, or the sole value if only one is present. Otherwise, selects the segment containing fAlpha and blends linearly between its endpoints.
requirements: Must have at least two values with strictly increasing weights to avoid division by zero and to define valid segments (inferred from the computation of sectionAlpha).
ValueType must support scalar multiplication by float and addition (i.e., ValueType * float and ValueType + ValueType must be valid).
fAlpha is typically in [0,1]; values outside this range extrapolate to the first/last segment endpoints as implemented.

functions.name: Framework::TimedLinearInterpolator::SetValues
functions.signature: template <typename BidirectionalRange> void Framework::TimedLinearInterpolator<ValueType>::SetValues(const BidirectionalRange &data, bool isLooping = true);
functions.description: Loads timed control values for interpolation. For each element in data, calls GetValue(elem) and GetTime(elem) to populate the internal value/weight list, asserts that each time/weight is in [0,1], optionally appends the first element to close a loop, and then forces the first and last weights to 0 and 1 respectively. Intended for subsequent interpolation via Interpolate.
requirements: BidirectionalRange must be iterable with begin()/end() and contain elements acceptable to GetValue() and GetTime().
GetTime(elem) must return a float in [0.0f, 1.0f] (asserted).
If isLooping is true and data is non-empty, the first element is appended to close the loop.

For meaningful interpolation and to avoid zero-length segments, the sequence of times should be monotonically non-decreasing and contain at least two distinct weights (inferred from Interpolate’s segment search and normalization).
ValueType must support the arithmetic required by Interpolate (addition and float scaling).

functions.name: Framework::LinearInterpolator::SetValues
functions.signature: template <typename BidirectionalRange> void Framework::LinearInterpolator<ValueType>::SetValues(const BidirectionalRange &data, bool isLooping = true);
functions.description: Loads untimed control values and assigns evenly spaced weights over [0,1]. Optionally duplicates the last value to close a loop (default true). Weights are computed as valIndex / (count-1).
requirements: BidirectionalRange must be iterable and yield elements convertible/assignable to ValueType.
If data is empty, the interpolator remains empty and no weights are computed.

If data contains exactly one element, either provide isLooping = true (default) so a duplicate is added, or ensure the range has at least two elements; otherwise a division by zero occurs when computing weights (denominator count-1 would be 0).
If looping is enabled, an extra value is appended duplicating the last element before weighting.
ValueType must support the arithmetic required by Interpolate (addition and float scaling).

functions.name: Framework::ConstVelLinearInterpolator::SetValues
functions.signature: template <typename BidirectionalRange> void Framework::ConstVelLinearInterpolator<ValueType>::SetValues(const BidirectionalRange &data, bool isLoop = true);
functions.description: Loads control values and computes cumulative distances between successive points using a free function distance(a,b) to produce weights that map interpolation to constant traversal speed. Optionally appends the first element to close a loop. Weights are then normalized by total path length to lie in [0,1].
requirements: BidirectionalRange must be iterable and yield elements convertible/assignable to ValueType.
A free function distance(const ValueType&, const ValueType&) returning float must be visible at the call site (ADL or namespace scope).
If isLoop is true, the first element is appended at the end to close the loop.

The total distance (sum of distances between successive points) must be greater than 0 to avoid division by zero during normalization. This implies at least two distinct points if there are two or more elements, and if a single element is provided, either disable looping or ensure distances are non-zero.
ValueType must support the arithmetic required by Interpolate (addition and float scaling).

functions.name: Framework::ConstVelLinearInterpolator::Distance
functions.description: Returns the total accumulated path length computed in the last SetValues call. If no values were loaded or all segment distances were zero, this will be 0.0f.
requirements: Meaningful (non-zero) distance requires that SetValues has been called with at least one non-zero-length segment.
